train.title: How Train works
train.b1: Your plan is a list of workout days. Up next is the day to do now.
train.b2: Tap Start to begin. You can do any day at any time: it still counts.
train.b3: The book button opens the exercise library. The clock shows your past workouts.

workout.title: During a workout
workout.b1: Check the weight and reps, then tap Done set. The rest timer starts by itself.
workout.b2: Swipe left or right to move between exercises. Nothing you typed is lost.
workout.b3: Tap Finish at the end. Only the sets you ticked are saved.

diet.title: How Diet works
diet.b1: Log what you eat in each meal: search, scan a barcode or pick a recent food.
diet.b2: The ring shows the kcal left today. The bars show protein, carbs and fat.
diet.b3: Tap the gear at the top to change your targets or switch to fixed meals.

progress.title: How Progress works
progress.b1: Add a check-in to save your weight, body fat, measurements and photos.
progress.b2: Your lines start after two check-ins. Once a week is enough.
progress.b3: Strength shows how much stronger you get, from the sets you log.

community.title: How the community works
community.b1: Leaderboards compare how much each person improves, not who is strongest.
community.b2: Others see only your name, level, scores and badges. Never your weight or photos.
community.b3: Tap ⓘ next to a leaderboard to see how its score is counted.

setsReps.title: Sets and reps
setsReps.body: A rep (repetition) is one lift: up and down once. A set is a group of reps done without stopping. You rest between sets.
setsReps.example: 3 × 10 means 3 sets of 10 reps: lift 10 times, rest, 10 more, rest, 10 more.

restTimer.title: Rest timer
restTimer.body: When you tick a set, a timer counts down your rest before the next one. Use −15 and +15 to change it, or Skip to go on now. Your phone tells you when the rest is over.
restTimer.example: Heavy sets of 5 reps often need 2 to 3 minutes. Lighter sets of 12 need about 1 minute.
restTimer.why: Resting long enough lets you lift well in the next set.

weightSuggestion.title: Next weight suggestion
weightSuggestion.body: The app looks at your last workout. If you reached the top of the rep range in every set, it adds a little weight; if you fell short, it lowers it a bit. Otherwise it keeps the weight and you aim for one more rep.
weightSuggestion.example: Target 6–8 reps. Last time 60 kg × 8 in every set, so today: 62.5 kg.
weightSuggestion.why: Adding a little weight or a rep over time is called progressive overload. It is how you get stronger.

e1rm.title: Estimated max (1RM)
e1rm.body: 1RM means one-rep max: the heaviest weight you could lift just once. You never have to try it. The app works it out from your sets of 12 reps or fewer.
e1rm.example: 60 kg for 10 reps gives an estimated max of 80 kg (60 × (1 + 10 ÷ 30)).
e1rm.why: You can compare workouts even when the weight or the reps change. If it goes up, you are getting stronger.

actualMax.title: Actual max
actualMax.body: The heaviest weight you really lifted in this exercise, for any number of reps, in a set you ticked as done.
actualMax.example: Sets of 80 kg × 5 and 85 kg × 2: your actual max is 85 kg.

records.title: Records
records.body: A record is a new personal best in an exercise: a heavier weight than ever before, or a higher estimated max.
records.example: Your best squat was 100 kg. Today you lift 102.5 kg: new record.
records.why: Records show your progress, and they earn XP and badges.

strengthScore.title: Strength score
strengthScore.body: How much your estimated max changed over the period, in %, averaged over your exercises. Exercises with more sets count more. Only exercises done on at least 2 different days count.
strengthScore.example: Bench press 80 → 84 kg (+5%) and squat 100 → 102 kg (+2%), with the same number of sets: about +3.5%.
strengthScore.why: One number that tells you whether your training is working.

volume.title: Volume
volume.body: Volume is all the weight you moved: weight × reps, added up for every set you finished.
volume.example: 3 sets of 10 reps at 50 kg = 1,500 kg of volume.
volume.why: More volume over the weeks usually means more work for your muscles.

hardSets.title: Hard sets and the guideline
hardSets.body: A hard set is a real working set, not a light warm-up. The main muscle of an exercise gets 1 set, a muscle that helps half a set and a muscle that steadies a quarter. Many studies suggest about 10 to 20 hard sets per muscle a week to build muscle.
hardSets.example: 4 sets of bench press = 4 chest sets, plus 2 for the front shoulders and 2 for the triceps.
hardSets.why: It shows which muscles get a lot of work and which get little, so your training stays balanced.

muscleLevels.title: Muscles worked
muscleLevels.body: Every exercise works one main muscle. Other muscles help it, and some only steady the body. For your weekly sets, the main muscle gets 1 set for each set you do, a muscle that helps gets half a set and a muscle that steadies gets a quarter.
muscleLevels.example: 4 sets of back squat = 4 sets for the quads, 2 for the glutes and 2 for the inner thighs, 1 for the hamstrings and 1 for the lower back.
muscleLevels.why: It shows how much work each muscle really gets, so your training balance is right.

plan.title: Workout plan
plan.body: A plan is your list of workout days, such as Push, Pull and Legs. Each day has its exercises, with sets, reps and rest. One plan is active at a time.
plan.example: A 3-day plan: Push on Monday, Pull on Wednesday, Legs on Friday.
plan.why: With a plan you never have to think about what to do next.

cycle.title: Cycle and up next
cycle.body: A cycle is one round through every day of your plan. Up next is the first day you have not done yet in this cycle. You can do any day at any time: it still counts. When every day is done, a new cycle starts.
cycle.example: Plan: Push, Pull, Legs. You did Push and Legs, so Up next is Pull. After Pull, cycle 2 starts.

dropSet.title: Drop sets
dropSet.body: After a set, lower the weight and keep going right away, with no rest. Each lighter round is a drop.
dropSet.example: Curls 14 kg × 10, then straight away 10 kg × 8, then 6 kg × 8.
dropSet.why: It works the muscle harder in less time. When you are starting out, use it on the last set only.

superset.title: Supersets
superset.body: Two or more exercises done in turn: one set of each, then one rest. They are labelled A1, A2 and so on.
superset.example: A1 curls × 10, A2 triceps pushdowns × 10, then rest 90 s. Do that 3 times.
superset.why: It saves time, and works well for muscles that do opposite jobs.

calorieTarget.title: Calorie target
calorieTarget.body: How many kcal (calories) to eat each day for your goal. Eating less than your body burns (a deficit) makes you lose weight. Eating more (a surplus) helps you build muscle. For your safety the target is never under 1,500 kcal or more than 25% under your maintenance.
calorieTarget.example: You burn about 2,500 kcal a day. To lose fat slowly, aim for about 2,250 (10% less).
calorieTarget.why: What you eat is the biggest part of changing your weight.

maintenance.title: Maintenance calories
maintenance.body: The kcal your body burns in a day: to stay alive, move and train. Eat this much and your weight stays about the same. The app estimates it from your sex, age, height, weight and daily activity.
maintenance.example: A man of 30, 180 cm, 80 kg, mostly sitting: about 2,150 kcal a day.
maintenance.why: It is only an estimate. If your weight changes while you eat this much, move your target by 100 to 200 kcal.

macros.title: Macros: protein, carbs and fat
macros.body: Macros are the three parts of food that give you energy: protein builds and repairs muscle, carbs are your main fuel for training, and fat keeps your hormones and body healthy. 1 g of protein or carbs = 4 kcal, 1 g of fat = 9 kcal.
macros.example: 2,000 kcal split 30% protein, 40% carbs, 30% fat = 150 g protein, 200 g carbs, 67 g fat.
macros.why: Enough protein helps you keep or build muscle, whatever your goal.

trainingBonus.title: Higher target on training days
trainingBonus.body: On days you log a workout, your calorie target goes up a little, and the extra kcal go to carbs. Rest days keep the normal target.
trainingBonus.example: Target 2,000 kcal. On a workout day it becomes 2,200: 200 kcal more, as 50 g of carbs.
trainingBonus.why: Training uses energy. More carbs on those days help you train and recover.

trackingMode.title: Count foods or fixed meals
trackingMode.body: Count foods: you log each food you eat, by search or barcode, and see what is left for the day. Fixed meals: you plan your meals once, then tick each one off when you eat it.
trackingMode.example: Count foods suits a varied diet. Fixed meals suits eating mostly the same things, like meal prep.
trackingMode.why: Both use the same targets, and you can switch any time.

bodyFat.title: Body fat %
bodyFat.body: The share of your weight that is fat. A smart scale, calipers or a tape measure can estimate it. Each gives a slightly different number, so use the same one every time.
bodyFat.example: 80 kg at 20% body fat = 16 kg of fat.
bodyFat.why: Weight alone can hide change: you can lose fat and gain muscle and weigh the same.

leanMass.title: Lean mass and fat mass
leanMass.body: Fat mass is the kg of fat in your body. Lean mass is everything else: muscle, bones, water and organs. Both come from your weight and body fat %.
leanMass.example: 80 kg at 20% body fat: 16 kg fat mass and 64 kg lean mass.
leanMass.why: Lean mass going up while fat mass goes down is the best kind of change.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.body: A check-in saves your weight, body fat, measurements and photos for the day. Every field is optional. Once a week, at the same time of day, works well.
checkIn.example: Every Monday before breakfast: weight, waist and three photos.
checkIn.why: Regular check-ins draw your lines in Progress.

streak.title: Streak
streak.body: Your streak is the number of days in a row you logged something: food, a workout or a check-in. Miss a whole day and it starts again from 0.
streak.example: You log Monday to Thursday: a 4-day streak. Nothing on Friday, so on Saturday it is back to 0.

xpLevels.title: XP and levels
xpLevels.body: XP (experience points) are points for what you do: logging, workouts, days on target, check-ins, records and badges. Enough XP takes you to the next level. Each level needs a bit more than the last.
xpLevels.example: A workout gives 50 XP, a day on your calorie target 20, a check-in 10. A day gives at most 100 XP. Level 2 needs 100 XP, level 3 another 150.

badgeRarity.title: Badges and rarity
badgeRarity.body: Badges reward milestones, like your first workout or 10 days in a row on your diet. Rare and epic ones need many days, or many days in a row. Streaks allow up to 2 off-target days a week if the week stays within 10% of its targets, and up to 2 rest days a week, never 2 in a row. Medals ask for diet, training, water goal and supplements on the same days.
badgeRarity.example: Iron medal: 10 days in a row with your diet, training, water goal and supplements all kept.

boardWorkouts.title: Workouts score
boardWorkouts.body: The number of workouts you finished this week or this month. At most 2 a day count.
boardWorkouts.example: Workouts on Monday, Wednesday and Friday = 3.

boardDiet.title: Diet score
boardDiet.body: The share of days you ate within 10% of your own calorie target. Only days with a target count. Everyone has their own target, so anyone can reach 100%.
boardDiet.example: Target 2,000 kcal: a day between 1,800 and 2,200 counts. 5 of 7 days = 71%.

boardTraining.title: Training score
boardTraining.body: The share of your planned workouts you did. A plan of 3 days counts as 3 workouts planned a week. Workouts outside a plan do not count here.
boardTraining.example: A 3-day plan and 2 plan workouts this week = 67%.

boardStrength.title: Strength score
boardStrength.body: How much your estimated max went up since the start of the period, in %. It is measured against where you started, so a beginner can beat a strong lifter.

plans.title: Free, Supporter and Premium
plans.body: Free has every feature. Supporter adds extras for people who want to back FFT, like comparing with friends and profile colours. Premium adds the AI coach with no key of your own, with a monthly allowance.
plans.example: With Free you can still use the coach with your own AI key, from Anthropic or another provider.

serverCopy.title: Copy on the server
serverCopy.body: Your data is always saved on this phone. A copy on our server (in the EU) lets you use the web app and other phones, connect AI apps, and get your data back if you lose your phone. You choose what goes, and can turn it off.
serverCopy.example: You lose your phone: sign in on a new one and everything comes back.

encryption.title: End-to-end encryption
encryption.body: Your data is locked on your phone before it is sent, with a key only you have (made from your passphrase). Our server keeps it but cannot read it.
encryption.example: Like a locked box: we carry it, but only you have the key.
encryption.why: If you lose both your passphrase and your recovery key, nobody can open the copy, not even us. The API and AI apps cannot use it.

relay.title: Sync with another phone
relay.body: Your phones send each other their changes through our server, locked with a key only your phones have. The server keeps nothing: each change is deleted once your other phone has it.
relay.example: You log lunch on your phone: it shows on your tablet a few seconds later.

apiMcp.title: API and MCP
apiMcp.body: The API lets your own programs read and change your FFT data. MCP is the way AI apps like Claude or ChatGPT connect to it. A token is a secret key for one tool: keep it private, and revoke it when you stop using it.
apiMcp.example: Connect Claude, then ask it: "How much protein did I eat this week?"

foodSource.title: Where the food data comes from
foodSource.body: Generic foods, like apple or rice, come from Ciqual: a food table from a French public agency (ANSES), with checked values per 100 g. Packaged products come from Open Food Facts: a free database filled in from product labels by volunteers. A green tick means the values were checked. Foods you create are only yours.
foodSource.example: Apple, raw (Ciqual): 54 kcal per 100 g. A cereal bar (Open Food Facts): found by its barcode.

previous.title: Previous
previous.body: What you did in this set the last time you did this exercise, so you know what to aim for. A dash (—) means there is no last time yet: it is your first time.
previous.example: Previous 60 × 8: last time you lifted 60 kg for 8 reps in this set.

consent.title: Your health data
consent.body: Weight, food, workouts and photos are health data. We use them only to run the app: on this phone and, if you keep a copy on our server (in the EU), there too. Other users cannot see them. Our team can technically reach the server copy and its backups; we look only when needed to fix a problem, and every look is logged. With end-to-end encryption on, nobody but you can read it. You can export or delete everything at any time in Settings > Your data.
consent.health: I agree to the processing of my health data
consent.healthDetail: Required: FFT cannot work without storing these data. If you do not agree, you cannot set up a profile, and nothing is stored. You can withdraw it later: the app pauses (you can still export or delete your data) and our server stops using it.

ai.title: Use FFT with your AI
ai.body: Optional: connect Claude or ChatGPT and ask them about your training and diet, or let them log food and plan workouts for you. They sign in with your FFT account.
ai.later: You can do this any time in Profile > API & MCP.

consent.title: Before you use the AI coach
consent.intro: The coach is an AI model. To answer you, the app has to send it what you write.
consent.whereIncluded: With the AI included in Premium, it goes through our server to OpenRouter (USA) and a provider that runs the AI model (now DeepSeek V4.1), picked among those that keep no data.
consent.whereOwn: With your own AI key, it goes straight from this device to the provider you chose ({{provider}}), under your agreement with them. Our server is not involved.
consent.what: What you write and the files and photos you attach are always sent: you choose them. Your stored data (body, diet, training, photos) is sent only for the kinds you allow below. They are all off until you turn them on.
consent.health: This can include health data, such as your weight, what you eat or your workouts.
consent.anonymous: It is sent without your name, email, account or device, and without your birth date (only your age, if you share your profile).
consent.noTraining: With the included AI, only providers that do not keep it and do not use it to train models are used.
consent.later: You can change what the coach sees in the AI coach settings, and withdraw this consent in Settings > Your data.
consent.declined: Nothing was sent. You can agree later in the AI coach settings.
consent.given: You agreed on {{date}}. Withdraw it in Settings > Your data.

serverCopy.means: A copy of the data you choose (body, diet, training, progress photos) and of your profile and settings is stored on our server in the EU. When you turn it off, that copy is deleted.
serverCopy.optionOn: Keep a copy on the server
serverCopy.optionOnDetail: Synced with the web app and your other devices; AI apps can connect.
serverCopy.optionOffDetail: Nothing is sent to our server. No web app and no AI apps, and if you lose this phone your data is lost too (Export keeps a backup).

serverCopy.failed: That did not work, nothing was changed. Check your connection and try again.
serverCopy.neededTitle: AI apps need the copy on the server

The web app, your other devices and AI apps no longer see it, and what they change in it does not reach this phone. You can turn it on again later: this phone then sends it again.

vault.title: End-to-end encryption
vault.onDetail: On: our server keeps only encrypted data it cannot read. API and AI apps are off.
vault.offDetail: Off: the copy on the server is readable by the server (needed by the API and AI apps).
vault.webNote: To turn it on or off, use the FFT app on your phone.
vault.lockedDetail: This device does not have your key yet: enter your passphrase to sync it.
vault.onTitle: Encrypt the copy on the server?
vault.onBody: Your data is encrypted on this phone before it is sent, with a key only you have. Our server keeps it but cannot read it.

onPoints.api: The API and AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, MCP) stop working while encryption is on: they read the copy on the server.
onPoints.admin: Nobody at FFT can see your data on the server, only how much there is and when it changed.
onPoints.lost: If you lose both your passphrase and your recovery key, the copy on the server cannot be read by anyone. Your phone keeps its data.
onPoints.devices: Your other phones and the web app ask for the passphrase once.

vault.passphraseHint: Not your login password. At least {{count}} characters; a few words are easy to remember.
vault.notSame: The two passphrases are not the same.
vault.recoveryBody: If you forget your passphrase, this key opens your data. It is shown only now: write it down or keep it in a password manager.
vault.turnedOn: The copy on the server is now end-to-end encrypted.
vault.offBody: Your data is sent to our server again in a readable form, so the API and AI apps can work. The encrypted copy and your key are then deleted from the server.
vault.turnedOff: Encryption is off. The copy on the server is being sent again.
vault.newPassphraseBody: Your data stays as it is: only the lock of your key changes. Your recovery key keeps working.
vault.unlockBody: Enter the passphrase you chose for encryption (not your login password) to open your data on this device.
vault.wrong: That is not the right passphrase.
vault.wrongRecovery: That is not the right recovery key.
vault.failed: That did not work, nothing was changed. Check your connection and try again.
vault.apiOffTitle: API and AI apps are off
vault.apiOffBody: Your copy on the server is end-to-end encrypted, so our server cannot read it for Claude, ChatGPT or your own tools. Turn encryption off in Settings > Your data to use them.

relay.title: Sync with another phone
relay.intro: Your phones exchange changes through our server, end-to-end encrypted with a key that only your phones have (it travels in the code, never to the server). The server keeps no copy: each change is deleted as soon as your other phone has it, and anything not delivered after 30 days.
relay.serverCopyOn: Your phones already sync through the copy on the server. To sync them without keeping a copy on the server, turn that copy off first: the two cannot be on together.
relay.webNote: Pairing phones is done in the FFT app on your phones.
relay.codeBody: On the other phone, signed in to the same account: Settings > Your data > Sync with another phone > Scan a code. Or type the code below.
relay.codeWarning: Anyone with this code and your account could read your data: show it only to your own phones.
relay.scanBody: Point the camera at the code shown on your other phone, or type it.
relay.needCamera: The camera is needed to scan the code. You can also type it.
relay.invalid: That is not a pairing code. Check it and try again.
relay.paired: This phone is paired. Your data is being exchanged.
relay.removeBody: It stops receiving your changes, and what was waiting for it on the server is deleted. Its own data stays on it. To pair it again, scan the code again.
relay.leaveBody: This phone stops sending and receiving changes. Its data stays on it, and the other phones keep theirs.
relay.left: This phone no longer syncs with your other phones.
relay.alwaysSent: Always exchanged: your profile, your settings and your consents. Everything is end-to-end encrypted.
relay.failed: That did not work. Check your connection and try again.
relay.joinBody: This account keeps its data only on your phones. Scan the code shown on your other phone (Settings > Your data > Sync with another phone) to bring your data here.
relay.waiting: Paired. Waiting for your other phone: keep FFT open on it.
relay.endsRelay: Your phones now sync through the encrypted relay. Keeping a copy on the server replaces it: the relay stops (each phone keeps its data).

look.intro: Make your community profile yours. Other members see it on leaderboards, in friends and on your profile.
look.entryInfo: Photo, colour, frame, title and badge
look.lockedBody: A profile photo, colours, frames, a title and a showcase badge come with Supporter and Premium.
look.joinBody: Your look is part of your community profile: join to choose it.
look.hiddenNote: Your plan has ended: others see the default look. Your choices are kept for when you come back.
look.photoPublic: Your photo is public to every community member. It is deleted when you remove it or leave the community.
look.photoFailed: The photo could not be uploaded. Check your connection and try again.
look.badgeInfo: One badge you earned, next to your name.
look.noBadges: Earn a badge and open Progress to show it here.
look.title: Title
look.titleInfo: A short title next to your name, from this list.
look.saveFailed: Could not save. Check your connection and try again.
look.photoReviewInfo: Some members reported it, so others see your initial for now. You can remove it, but not change it until the review is done.
look.photoBanned: You can no longer add a profile photo
look.photoBannedInfo: Three of your photos were judged inappropriate. Your colour, frame, title and badge still work.

report.title: Report this photo?
report.body: Tell us if {{name}}'s profile photo is not right for the community. They will not know who reported it. After a few reports the photo is hidden until we review it.
report.gone: This photo has changed or is no longer shown.
report.tooMany: You sent many reports today. Try again tomorrow.
report.failed: Could not send the report. Check your connection and try again.

community.needsAccountInfo: Leaderboards are shared through our server, so they need an account. Everything else keeps working on this phone.
community.error: Could not reach the community. Check the connection and try again.

join.title: Join the community
join.intro: Leaderboards anyone can win: each score is measured against where you started, not against how strong you are.
join.changeInfo: Changing it here changes your profile name everywhere.
join.leaveInfo: You can leave at any time from your community profile.
join.noName: Add your name first: others see it on the leaderboards.

audienceDetail.class: Your age group and weight class

filters.title: Compare with

filters.notePaid: Places are counted among the people you pick.

empty.friendsBody: None of your friends has a score yet. Add friends to compare with people you know.

no_country.title: No country yet
no_country.body: Your country comes from your phone's region. Set it in the phone's settings, then open Progress again.

no_class.title: Age group or weight class unknown
no_class.body: Add your birth date and sex in Personal info and log your weight to compare with your class.

info.diet: Share of days within 10% of each person's own calorie target since {{date}}.
info.training: Share of each person's own planned workouts done since {{date}}.
info.strength: Change in estimated max since {{date}}. Measured against where each person started, so anyone can win.

you.noScore: You have no score here yet
you.noScoreInfo: Train or log this period to get one.

friends.title: Friends
friends.none: No friends yet. Share your code, or add someone's.

profile.note: This is how others see you
profile.noteInfo: They also get an Add friend button here.
profile.privacy: Others see only your name, level, scores and badges. Never your weight, measurements or photos.
profile.leaveInfo: Your member profile (with your photo and look), scores and friends are deleted from our server now. You can join again later, as a new member.
profile.rejoined: You are back in the community. Friends need to be added again.

code.title: Your friend code
code.info: Friends type this code in "Add a friend". It only lets people send you a request.
code.qrA11y: QR code of your friend code {{code}}
code.label: Friend code
